title: I have a bunch of old Flash style line art I would to feed to a AI tool so it could try and make art in this style.
author: PlaidWorld
selftext:
I have a bunch of old Flash style line art I would to feed to a AI tool so it could try and make art in this style. 

What tools should I be looking at for this kind of thing?

comments.author: Juzzaman
comments.body: Train a lora for an image model like Illustrious or Chroma my dude

replies.author: PlaidWorld
replies.body: Thanks. I will note this down.

comments.author: MisterReigns
comments.body: Throw it into ChatGPT and tell it what style you want it in or just tell it to remake it in 3D or whatever.  Works really well.  Free version will do this.

replies.author: PlaidWorld
replies.body: I fed it a rough fish and it gave me a beautiful and completely useable pixel art fish..I am really surprised.

replies.author: PlaidWorld
replies.body: I was told AI can't do pixel art at all... maybe everyone meant animations?

replies.author: eugene20
replies.body: A lot of people struggled to get pixel art working because it would give partial pixels, but there have been trained models or lora's since that worked fine. Hunt around and I'm sure you would fine something, people use them for rapid spite sheets for example.

replies.author: MisterReigns
replies.body: Check out replicate.com.  It requires a GitHub account and it costs pennies per run, but once there search for "image to video", then throw that fish in there and give it a prompt; something like "make this fish swim, solid black background" and it will do it.  I say add the background because you can break down the frames into .png files with other sites then remove the background and have a swimming fish for a game.  Kewl stuff.
